By the mere hearing of whose name, the all-pervading Lord of All,
great sins are destroyed—may that Lord of All abide in your heart!’
Hearing this succession of blessings, you, king Vṛddhakāla,
will then remember this incident, your body covered in goosebumps.

4.24.m: Concealing your emotion, giving much wealth to them,
and waiting for an auspicious moment, after bestowing the kingdom upon your son,
you will then depart for Kāśī along with queen Anaṅgalekhā.
Having given abundant gifts and satisfied those who ask,
and having established there a liṅga under your own name, which causes nirvāṇa,
having built a lofty temple there and, in front of it, an excellent well,
having duly performed the installation of the pinnacle and other [rites] there,
having given wealth in jewels, rubies, gold, fine silks, elephants, horses, and cattle,
and large banners, flags, parasols, chowries, and mirrors,
having bestowed abundant equipment for the god, untiring,
your body emaciated through vows, fasts, and observances,
at midday in that deserted place you will see an ascetic:
with an extremely aged body, having reddish matted hair,
tall, like Dharma incarnate, charming to people,
resting the weight of his staff-like body upon a firm staff,
emerging from the inner sanctum and approaching the theater pavilion.
Sitting down beside you, he will ask you thus in order:

4.24.m: Questioned thus by the aged ascetic, O Lord,
you will say: “I am a king, known as Vṛddhakāla,
a southerner, arrived here together with this beloved wife.
I meditate on this liṅga, and I ask for nothing.
O ascetic with matted hair, Śiva himself is the builder of this temple.
In particular, I do not know for certain the name of this liṅga.”
Hearing these words of the king, the ascetic with matted hair said:

4.24.m: and I also know this devoted wife of yours.

By him she was given in marriage to the noble-minded Naidhruva;
and that Naidhruva fell under the power of Time before reaching youth.
Observing widowhood, keeping auspicious vows, she died in Avantī.

Wedded by you, O King, ever devoted to her husband,

4.24.m: or in Dvāravatī, or in Kāñcī, or in Māyāpurī, O King,

4.24.d: अपि पातकिनो ये च कालेन निधनं गताः ..
4.24.m: even sinners who meet their death in the course of time—
they, coming here from heaven, will indeed attain liberation in Kāśī.
I know you too, O King: in your previous birth you were a brahmin,
a native of Mathurā named Śivaśarman, and you died in Māyāpurī.
Having attained Vaikuṇṭha through that merit and enjoyed delightful pleasures,
from the remainder of that merit you were born as a king in Nandivardhana.
O protector of the earth of Vṛddhakāla, by that very good deed,
you have reached this sacred field of liberation and will attain unsurpassed liberation. (67)
Moreover, listen, O king of kings, to what was spoken by you:
'Śambhu is the maker and the one who causes the temple to be made'—that is plainly true. (68)
A good deed should never be constantly proclaimed;
from saying 'this was done by me', merit vanishes that very instant. (69)
Therefore, with every effort, it must be concealed like a treasure;
a good deed becomes futile by boasting, just like an oblation offered into ashes. (70)
Prompted indeed by Viśvanātha, O sinless one,
the temple and the rest have been built here by you whose purpose is accomplished; so I know. (71)
This liṅga, O king, named Vṛddhakāleśvara,
know to be established from beginningless time, yet you indeed were the instrumental cause. (72)
From seeing, touching, worshipping, hearing of, and bowing to
this liṅga of Vṛddhakāleśa, one obtains everything desired. (73)
The well named Kālodaka destroys old age and disease;
by drinking its water, one never drinks mother’s milk again. (74)
Having bathed in the well's water and worshipped this liṅga,
a person attains within a year the perfection desired by the mind. (75)

4.24.m: Before your eyes, my old age and grey hair duly
perished in a moment through drinking the water of this well, and I became young again. (79)
When the liṅga Vṛddhakāleśvara is worshipped, there is no poverty,

To the north of Kṛttivāsa in Vārāṇasī, with diligence,
the Vṛddhakāleśvara liṅga must be beheld by those who desire siddhi. (81)

4.24.m: Having spoken thus and grasped that king by the hand, the ascetic,
along with Queen Anaṅgalekhā, entered dissolution into that liṅga. (82)
From proclaiming, 'O Mahākāla, O Mahākāla, O Mahākāla!',
one is freed a hundredfold from sins; no doubt should be entertained here. (83)
In this manner, liberation will be yours after the darśana of the enemy of Kaiṭabha,
having enjoyed diverse pleasures in the auspicious city of Vaikuṇṭha. (84)

4.24.d: इति संहृष्टतनूरुहः स विप्रो भगवत्तद्गणवक्त्रतो निशम्य ..
4.24.m:
Thus, with hair bristling with joy, having heard [this] from the mouth of that attendant of the Lord,
the brahmin beheld his own future in Hari's realm, delightful as ten million suns. (85)
Maitrāvaruṇi said:
O Lopāmudrā, that best of brahmins, having enjoyed delightful pleasures,
and by the power of the merit of relinquishing his life in Māyāpurī, (86)
came from the realm of Vaikuṇṭha to the city of Nandivardhana,
enjoyed earthly pleasures, fathered handsome sons, (87)
and, transferring the kingdom to them, reached the city of Vārāṇasī,

4.24.s: teṣu rājyaṃ vinikṣipya prāpya vārāṇasīṃ purīm ..
4.24.d: तेषु राज्यं विनिक्षिप्य प्राप्य वाराणसीं पुरीम् ..
4.24.m: where, having worshipped Viśveśvara, he attained the state of nirvāṇa. (88)
Having heard this most sacred narrative of the brahmin Śivaśarman,
a person is freed from sin and attains supreme knowledge. (89)

4.24.m:
Vyāsa said:
Listen, Sūta, I will recount the story of the pot-born [sage],
hearing which a man becomes free from passion and a vessel of knowledge. (1)
Having circumambulated the mountain named Śrī,
the pot-born one, together with his wife, then beheld the vast, charming grove of Skanda, (2)
filled with flowers in all seasons, with trees bearing succulent fruits,
rich in edible roots and tubers, with trees having excellent bark, (3)
frequented by herds of wild beasts, surrounded by rivers and pools,
with clear and deep lakes, the supreme essence of all the earth, (4)
resounding with various birds, inhabited by diverse sages,
as if it were the sole gathering-place of austerity and the abode of prosperity. (5)
There is a mountain there named Lohita, possessing the splendour of the golden mountain,
with lovely caves and waterfalls, its ridges shining like peaks, (6)
as if it were a single piece of Kailāsa that had descended here into the realm of action
to practice austerity intensely, endowed with many wonders. (7)
There the best of sages, Agastya, beheld the six-faced one in person.
Having bowed prostrate on the ground together with his wife, the one of great austerity (8)
praised the son of Girijā with hymns originating from the Vedas
and with a hymn of his own composition, with his hands folded in reverence. (9)
Agastya said:
Salutations to the one whose lotus feet are worshipped by the host of gods, who creates nectar,
who has six faces, boundless valour, and is the source of joy to Gaurī’s heart! (10)
Salutations to you, who removes the distress of the surrendered, the fulfiller of all wishes,
the granter of chariots for crossing over, the slayer of the fierce demon Tāraka! (11)
To the unformed yet formed, of a thousand forms, possessing qualities, the locus of qualities, higher than the high,
beyond the boundless shore, beyond the prior and the posterior, salutations to you whose mount is the peacock! (12)
Salutations to you, the best among knowers of Brahman, clad in space, abiding in the firmament,
golden-hued, golden-armed; salutations to the golden one, the golden-seeded! (13)
To the one whose nature is austerity, rich in austerity, the bestower of the fruits of austerity...

4.25.m: Vyāsa said: / "Listen, O Sūta, I shall tell the story of the pot-born sage, / hearing which a man becomes free from passion and a vessel of knowledge. / Having circumambulated the mountain named Śrī, the pot-born sage, / accompanied by his wife, then beheld the vast, delightful forest of Skanda, / filled with flowers in all seasons and with trees bearing luscious fruits, / pleasant to dwell in, rich in roots and tubers, with trees possessing fine bark, / frequented by herds of wild beasts, surrounded by rivers and pools, / with clear, deep lakes, the highest essence of the whole earth, / filled with the cries of various birds, inhabited by diverse sages, / like a single designated abode of austerity, an abode of auspicious treasures. / There is a mountain there named Lohita, resembling the Golden Mountain, / with excellent caves and waterfalls, shining with its peaks and slopes, / like a single fragment of Kailāsa that had arrived here in the land of ritual action, / as if to perform austere tapas, endowed with many wonders. / There Agastya, the best among sages, saw the six-faced one face to face; / prostrating like a stick upon the earth together with his wife, the one of great tapas / praised the son of the mountain-born goddess with hymns arising from the Vedic scriptures, / and also with a eulogy composed by himself, folding his hands in reverence. / Agastya said: / 'Homage be to the lotus feet praised by the multitude of immortals, the maker of nectar, / to the six-faced one of boundless valour, the born joy of Gaurī's heart! / Homage to you, the dispeller of distress of those who bow, the accomplisher of all desires, / the giver of chariots, the rescuer of others, the slayer of the fierce asura Tāraka! / To the unmanifest and manifest, to the thousand-formed, to virtue and the possessor of qualities, to the higher than the high, / to the shore of the shoreless, to the superior and inferior, homage to you whose mount is the peacock! "Salutations to the one who is forever a youth, the enemy of Himāramā, the detached one who made sovereignty seem like a blade of grass! 14

Kārtikeya said:
"Is all well, O pot-born sage, the sole helper of the gods? / I know that you have arrived here, as well as the heightening of the Vindhya mountain. 19
In Avimukta, the great sacred field protected by the three-eyed Lord, all is well— / where to those whose lifespan is exhausted, the odd-eyed Lord himself directly bestows liberation. 20
Neither on the surface of earth, heaven, or the atmosphere, nor at the base of Pātāla, nor even above / in the upper world, O sage, have I seen anywhere such a sacred field. 21
Even I, wandering alone here, in order to attain that sacred field, O sage, / perform austerities; yet even today my desires have not borne fruit. 22
Not by merits, nor by gifts, nor by austerities, nor by recitations of mantras, / nor is it obtainable by various sacrifices; it is obtainable only through the grace of the Lord. 23

It is a completely different creation of the Creator, one that surpasses [all else], / since even the Lord himself is scarcely able to describe the virtues of that sacred field. 25
Ah, the utter weakness of the intellect! Ah, the poverty of fortune! / Ah, the power of delusion, that Kāśī is not served here! 26
The body is continually worn away, and the sense-faculties also decay;

austerities of various kinds, observances, restraints, and disciplines; / confluences of rivers, and many forests; 37
mental [sacred fords], earthly ones, waterfalls and the like; / saline lands, seats of power, and the uninterrupted recitation of sacred scripture; 38

This sacred field alone is the cause for inquiring after your welfare. / Come, come, give me the touch of your own body, O you of noble vows! 44

Having spoken thus and touched all the limbs of the pot-born sage, / Skanda felt pleasure as if plunging into the waters of a lake of nectar. 50

4.25.m: Hear that māhātmya, O sinless sage, as it is told by me: / Avimukta is declared here to be the supreme secret of secrets; / perfection is present there, and the all-pervading Lord resides there perpetually. / That sacred field is not connected to the earthly plane, but moves in the atmosphere; / non-yogins do not behold it, while yogins indeed see it. / A person who dwells there, O brahmin, self-controlled and concentrated, / even though eating thrice a day, becomes equal to one who lives on air alone. / One who has great devotion in Avimukta even for the duration of a blink, / has performed great austerity accompanied by celibacy. / A steadfast man who dwells [there] for a month, taking light food and subduing his senses, / has performed the entirety of the divine Pāśupata observance. / Residing there for a year, having conquered anger and controlled the senses, / not nourishing his limbs with others' wealth, avoiding food from others, / free from slandering others, and devoted to giving even a little, / he has performed great austerity equal to a thousand years elsewhere. / A man knowing the māhātmya of the sacred field who dwells there all his life, / abandoning fear of birth and death, attains the supreme destination. / That state which cannot be obtained elsewhere even in hundreds of other births by yogas, / is easily attained here through the grace of the Lord. / Even a slayer of a brahmin who happens by destiny to reach the city of Vārāṇasī, / is freed from the sin of slaying a brahmin by the māhātmya of that sacred field. / As long as one does not abandon Avimukta until the fall of the body, / not only the slaying of a brahmin, but material nature itself ceases [for him]. / He who, single-minded, does not abandon that sacred field, / abandons old age, death, and the unbearable dwelling in a womb. / A wise man should dwell in Avimukta, which is frequented by hosts of gods and seers, / if he desires not to be born again on earth. / One should not abandon Avimukta, which frees from the fear of transmigration; / having reached the god Viśveśvara, he is not born again.

4.25.m: Even after committing thousands of sins, becoming a piśāca here is preferable, / but heaven, attainable through hundreds of sacrifices, is not [desirable] without the city of Kāśī. / At the time of departure, when the vital points of men are pierced, / tormented by wind, memory does not arise at all. / But there, at the time of departure, Viśveśvara himself directly / imparts the liberating Brahman, by which one becomes identified with it. / Knowing this human existence to be impermanent and full of many offenses, / one should reside in Avimukta, which destroys the fear of transmigration.

4.27.d: सर्वस्यार्ति हरे देवि नारायणि नमोस्तु ते .. 71 ..
4.27.m: O goddess Nārāyaṇī who remove the affliction of all, homage to you! // 71
Homage, homage to you, spotless, destroyer of difficulties, capable one,
and transcendent beyond the higher and the lower, O Gaṅgā, giver of nirvāṇa! // 72

4.27.s: gaṃge mamāgrato bhūyā gaṃge me tiṣṭha pṛṣṭhataḥ ..
4.27.d: गंगे ममाग्रतो भूया गंगे मे तिष्ठ पृष्ठतः ..
4.27.m: May you be before me, O Gaṅgā; O Gaṅgā, stay behind me!

4.27.s:
gaṃge me pārśvayoredhi gaṃge tvayyastu me sthitiḥ .. 73 . .
ādau tvamaṃte madhye ca sarvaṃ tvaṃ gāṃ gate śive ..
4.27.d:
गंगे मे पार्श्वयोरेधि गंगे त्वय्यस्तु मे स्थितिः .. 73 . .
आदौ त्वमंते मध्ये च सर्वं त्वं गां गते शिवे ..
4.27.m:
O Gaṅgā, be at my sides; O Gaṅgā, let my abode be in you! // 73
You are in the beginning, at the end, and in the middle; you are everything, O auspicious one who have descended to earth.
You alone are primordial nature (mūlaprakṛti); you indeed are the supreme Puruṣa.

4.27.s: gaṃge tvaṃ paramātmā ca śivasvatubhyaṃ namaḥ śive .. 74 ..
4.27.d: गंगे त्वं परमात्मा च शिवस्वतुभ्यं नमः शिवे .. 74 ..
4.27.m: O Gaṅgā, you are the supreme self and Śiva; homage to you, O auspicious one! // 74

4.27.s: ya idaṃ paṭhate stotraṃ śṛṇuyācchraddhayāpi yaḥ ..
4.27.d: य इदं पठते स्तोत्रं शृणुयाच्छ्रद्धयापि यः ..
4.27.m: Whoever recites this hymn of praise, or even hears it with faith,
is freed tenfold from sins arising from body, speech, and mind. // 75
A diseased person is freed from disease, and one beset with misfortunes from calamities;
the bound is freed from bondage, and the terrified is thoroughly freed from fear. // 76
He obtains all desires, and having died, goes to heaven,
mounted upon a celestial aerial chariot, fanned by divine women. // 77

4.27.s: gṛhepi likhitaṃ yasya sadā tiṣṭhati dhāritama ..
4.27.d: गृहेपि लिखितं यस्य सदा तिष्ठति धारितम ..
4.27.m: In whose house it remains preserved in writing at all times,

4.27.s: nāgnicorabhayaṃ tasya na sarpādi bhayaṃ kvacita .. 78 ..
4.27.d: नाग्निचोरभयं तस्य न सर्पादि भयं क्वचित .. 78 ..
4.27.m: for him there is no danger from fire or thieves, nor any danger from serpents and the like. // 78

4.27.s: jyeṣṭhe māse site pakṣe daśamī hastasaṃyutā ..
4.27.d: ज्येष्ठे मासे सिते पक्षे दशमी हस्तसंयुता ..
4.27.m: In the bright fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha, the tenth day joined with the Hasta asterism,
when joined with a Wednesday, destroys threefold sin. // 79
Standing in the waters of the Gaṅgā on that tenth day,

4.27.s:
yaḥ paṭheddaśakṛtvastu daridro vāpi cākṣamaḥ .. 4.1.27.180 . .
sopi tatphalamāpnoti gaṃgāṃ saṃpūjya yatnataḥ ..
4.27.d:
यः पठेद्दशकृत्वस्तु दरिद्रो वापि चाक्षमः .. 4.1.27.180 . .
सोपि तत्फलमाप्नोति गंगां संपूज्य यत्नतः ..
4.27.m:
whoever recites this hymn ten times, even if poor or incapable, / 4.1.27.180
he too attains that fruit, having worshipped the Gaṅgā with care.
Whatever fruit has been proclaimed by the previously stated procedure, [he attains it]. // 81

4.27.s: yathā gaurī tathā gaṃgā tasmādgauryāstu pūjane ..
4.27.d: यथा गौरी तथा गंगा तस्माद्गौर्यास्तु पूजने ..
4.27.m: As is Gaurī, so is the Gaṅgā; therefore, in the worship of Gaurī
whatever procedure is properly prescribed, that same applies to the worship of the Gaṅgā. // 82

4.27.s: yathā'haṃ tvaṃ tathā viṣṇo yathā tvaṃ tu tathāhyumā ..
4.27.d: यथाऽहं त्वं तथा विष्णो यथा त्वं तु तथाह्युमा ..
4.27.m: As I am, so are you, O Viṣṇu; as you are, so indeed is Umā;

4.27.s: umā yathā tathā gaṃgā catūrūpaṃ na bhidyate .. 83 ..
4.27.d: उमा यथा तथा गंगा चतूरूपं न भिद्यते .. 83 ..
4.27.m: as Umā is, so is the Gaṅgā: their fourfold form is not divided. // 83
A distinction between Viṣṇu and Rudra, and likewise a distinction between Śrī and Gaurī,

4.27.s: gaṃgāgauryaṃtaraṃ caiva yo brūte mūḍhadhīstu saḥ .. 84 ..
4.27.d: गंगागौर्यंतरं चैव यो ब्रूते मूढधीस्तु सः .. 84 ..
4.27.m: and also a distinction between Gaṅgā and Gaurī: whoever asserts [these] is dull-witted. // 84

4.27.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇe ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ caturthe kāśīkhaṃḍe pūrvārddhe gaṃgāmahimavarṇanapūrvaka daśaharā stotrakathanaṃnāma saptaviṃśatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 27 ..
4.27.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणे एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थे काशीखंडे पूर्वार्द्धे गंगामहिमवर्णनपूर्वक दशहरा स्तोत्रकथनंनाम सप्तविंशतितमोऽध्यायः .. 27 ..
4.27.m: Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Narration of the Daśaharā Hymn of Praise Preceded by the Description of the Greatness of the Gaṅgā,” in the first half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the fourth [section] of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand verses. // 27
